title: Vis Croatia Parking & Apartments Guide 2027
metaDescription: Complete 2027 guide to parking in Vis, Croatia. Find daily rates, zones, ferry port parking, and top-rated apartments offering free private parking.
content:
## Understanding the Parking Infrastructure in Vis Town

Vis town is the primary entry point to the island of Vis, accessible via the Jadrolinija ferry from Split. The town is geographically split into two main sections: Luka, which surrounds the ferry port, and Kut, the older historical area situated at the far end of the bay. Both areas feature narrow, historic streets that are often inaccessible to vehicles, making parking a central logistical challenge for visitors.

Public parking in Vis town operates on a zonal system. During the peak summer season, which runs from June 1st to September 30th, parking enforcement is strict, and capacity is frequently maxed out by mid-morning. The local municipal company, Gradina Vis, manages the public lots and street parking zones. 

### Luka (Ferry Port) Parking Zone

The largest public parking area in Vis town is located directly adjacent to the Jadrolinija ferry terminal in the Luka district. This lot accommodates approximately 100 to 120 vehicles. 

During the 2027 summer season, the rates for this primary lot are expected to be €2.00 per hour. A daily ticket, which allows for 24 hours of parking, costs €20.00. Payment can be made using coins at the physical meters, but the most efficient method is via mobile application. Because of its proximity to the ferry, grocery stores (like Tommy and Studenac), and local administrative offices, this lot experiences high turnover during the day but fills up completely overnight with tourists staying in nearby accommodations.

### Kut Parking Zone

For visitors staying in the Kut area of Vis town, a dedicated public parking lot is situated just behind the main waterfront, near the local school and football field. This lot is slightly cheaper, generally priced at €1.50 per hour or €15.00 for a 24-hour period. 

Kut is entirely pedestrianized along the immediate waterfront. Vehicles are not permitted to drive past the designated drop-off points near the restaurants. If your accommodation is in Kut, this lot is the only legal option for overnight parking unless your rental provides private space.

## Payment Methods and Enforcement

Croatia has largely digitized its parking payment systems. While physical ticket machines are still present in Vis, they often require exact change in euros.

### Digital Apps and SMS

The most reliable way to pay for parking across the island is the Bmove app (formerly known as PayDo). This application covers almost all municipal parking zones in Croatia, including Vis and Komiža. Users can link a credit card, select their zone via GPS, and purchase hourly or daily tickets without needing to return to their vehicle.

Alternatively, if you have a Croatian SIM card, you can use the SMS parking system. Signs in each parking lot display a specific shortcode (usually a five-digit number). Sending an SMS with your license plate number to this code purchases one hour of parking. A confirmation text serves as your digital receipt.

### Fines and Towing

Parking enforcement officers patrol the public lots in Vis town regularly between 7:00 AM and 11:00 PM. If you park in a paid zone without a valid ticket, an officer will place a daily parking ticket under your windshield wiper. This essentially acts as a fine, requiring you to pay the full 24-hour rate (typically €20.00 to €25.00 depending on the zone) within eight days. 

Parking in loading zones, blocking residential driveways in narrow streets, or leaving your vehicle in emergency access routes will result in immediate towing. The impound lot is located on the outskirts of Vis town, and retrieving a towed vehicle costs upwards of €150.00, plus the daily parking fine.

## Apartments with Guaranteed Parking in Vis Town

Many accommodation listings on platforms advertise 'street parking nearby.' This works well in theory, but reality is different during July and August when finding an available public spot becomes nearly impossible. Relying on public parking also adds €15 to €20 per day to your travel budget. Securing an apartment with guaranteed, on-site private parking is highly recommended.

Here are highly rated apartments and guesthouses in Vis town that provide dedicated parking spaces for their guests:

### Apartments Bilić

Located approximately 300 meters from the ferry port, Apartments Bilić offers a highly practical location for visitors arriving by car. The property provides a private, off-street parking area specifically reserved for guests. Rooms run between €90 and €120 per night during the summer. The location allows guests to leave their car securely parked while walking to the main restaurants, bakeries, and boat excursion departure points in Luka.

### Apartments & Rooms As

Situated slightly elevated above the main harbor, this property offers clear views of the bay and includes free private parking on the premises. Prices range from €110 to €150 per night. Because it is located slightly up the hill, the parking area is spacious enough for standard SUVs, which is a significant advantage on an island where tight driveways are the norm.

### Villa Bellevue Vis

For those seeking accommodation closer to the Kut area, Villa Bellevue Vis provides premium apartments with dedicated parking. Navigating to the parking area requires driving up a slight incline behind the main town road, but the private spots eliminate the need to compete for space in the public Kut lot. Rates generally span from €180 to €250 per night. The walk down to the Kut waterfront takes less than five minutes.

## Bringing a Car vs. Renting Locally

The logistics of getting a car to Vis require planning. The Jadrolinija car ferry from Split to Vis takes approximately two hours and twenty minutes. During the high season, the cost for a standard passenger car is roughly €45 to €55 one-way, plus around €8 per adult passenger. 

The ferry capacity is limited. In July and August, you must purchase your vehicle ticket days in advance and arrive at the Split port at least 60 to 90 minutes before departure to guarantee your vehicle gets loaded.

If you are visiting Vis for fewer than three days, do not bring a car on the ferry. Save your money here and spend it on something better, like a private boat tour to the Blue Cave or a meal at a local tavern. Local rental agencies near the Vis ferry port offer scooters starting at €30 per day and small cars for €60 to €80 per day. Renting locally removes the stress of ferry logistics and the high cost of transportation.

## Parking at Vis Island Beaches

Driving is the most efficient way to explore the island's famous beaches, but parking infrastructure varies significantly from bay to bay.

### Stiniva Beach

Stiniva is the most famous beach on Vis. Driving to Stiniva requires navigating the main central road across the island before turning onto a narrow access road. There is a designated dirt parking lot at the top of the cliff, managed by locals, which costs around €5.00 for the day. From the parking lot, visitors must hike down a very steep, rugged path for 20 to 30 minutes to reach the beach. Vehicles cannot access the beach directly.

### Srebrna Beach

Located near the village of Rukavac on the southeastern side of the island, Srebrna features a large, mostly unpaved parking area situated under pine trees. Parking here is generally free, though capacity fills quickly by 10:00 AM in the high season. From the parking area, it is a flat, 10-minute walk along a paved path to the pebble beach.

### Stončica Beach

Stončica is a sandy beach on the eastern coast. The road down to Stončica ends at a small, uneven dirt parking area. Parking is free but highly limited to roughly 20 cars. Once parked, visitors must walk along a dirt trail for about 15 minutes to reach the beach and the nearby tavern (Konoba Stončica).

## Parking in Komiža

Komiža is the second-largest town on the island, located on the western coast, precisely 10 kilometers from Vis town. The drive takes about 15 minutes via the D117 state road.

Komiža has implemented a strict traffic policy: the entire town center and harbor are closed to non-resident vehicles. Visitors driving to Komiža must park at the massive municipal parking lot located at the town's entrance, situated on a hill overlooking the bay. 

This lot has a capacity of over 300 vehicles. The pricing in 2027 is set at €2.00 per hour or €20.00 for a daily ticket. From the parking lot, it is a downhill walk of 5 to 10 minutes to reach the waterfront, restaurants, and the main harbor where Blue Cave tours depart. There is a small drop-off zone near the bus station, but parking there is strictly limited to 15 minutes.

## Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure

As electric vehicle (EV) adoption increases, Vis has slowly upgraded its infrastructure. There is an active EV charging station located in Vis town, positioned near the main ferry port parking lot. It features two Type 2 connections. 

Komiža also hosts one EV charging point near its main public parking area. Both stations are integrated into the standard Croatian charging networks (such as ELEN). However, because there are only a handful of plugs on the entire island, EV drivers should not rely solely on public chargers and should confirm charging availability with their apartment host prior to arrival.

## Scooter and Quad Bike Parking

Due to the narrow roads and limited car parking, many visitors opt to rent 50cc or 125cc scooters, or quad bikes. Vis town and Komiža provide designated, free parking zones specifically for two-wheeled vehicles. 

In Vis town, a large scooter parking area is located right next to the Jadrolinija ticket office. In Komiža, scooter parking is available much closer to the pedestrian zone than car parking. Do not park scooters in designated car spots within paid lots, as this can still result in a fine. Always use the specific free zones marked for motorcycles and scooters.

faq.question: How much does public parking cost in Vis town?
faq.answer: Public parking in Vis town typically costs between €1.50 and €2.00 per hour during the summer season. A daily ticket for 24 hours costs between €15.00 and €20.00, depending on the specific zone.

faq.question: Can I park my car for free in Vis town?
faq.answer: Free street parking is nearly non-existent in Vis town during the summer. Unless your accommodation provides a private parking space, you must use the municipal paid lots.

faq.question: Is it better to rent a car or bring one on the ferry to Vis?
faq.answer: For trips shorter than three days, renting a car or scooter locally is cheaper and easier. Bringing a car on the ferry costs approximately €45-€55 each way and requires arriving hours early during high season.

faq.question: Can I drive directly to Stiniva beach?
faq.answer: No, you cannot drive directly to the water at Stiniva. You must park at the cliff-top dirt lot (around €5.00 per day) and hike down a steep, rocky path for 20 to 30 minutes.

faq.question: Where do I park when visiting Komiža?
faq.answer: The center of Komiža is closed to visitor vehicles. You must park at the large municipal lot at the town's upper entrance, which costs €2.00 per hour or €20.00 per day, and walk down to the center.

faq.question: How do I pay for parking on Vis island?
faq.answer: You can pay using coins at physical parking meters or digitally via the Bmove (formerly PayDo) mobile application. If you have a Croatian phone number, you can also pay via SMS using the code on the parking signs.

quickAnswer: Parking in Vis town is divided into public zones, with peak summer rates between €1.50 and €2.00 per hour or €15 to €20 daily. The main lot is at the ferry port. Booking an apartment with guaranteed private parking is highly recommended to avoid daily fees and limited availability.
